candidates.response:
我用纯 SVG 手绘了整个场景——一只迎着落日骑行的鹈鹕，喙里还叼着一条露尾巴的小鱼，车子是深梅紫色的城市单车，铜铃挂在弯把上。所有运动（辐条、曲柄、双腿踩踏、波光、视差草丛）由一个 rAF 循环统一驱动，双腿用两连杆逆运动学求解，是真实地"踩"在踏板上的。 ```html 向晚 · 鹈鹕骑行
向 晚 A PELICAN AT DUSK
点击任意处 · 听一声铜铃
``` **实现要点：** - **真实踩踏**：双腿不是贴图式摆动，而是每帧用两连杆逆运动学解算（髋→膝→踝），膝盖取朝向车尾的解，是鸟类的关节姿态；齿比联动让曲柄、辐条、链条虚线保持物理一致的转速。 - **辐条与铜铃**：每轮 10 根银灰辐条高速旋转，附一层半透明"辐条盘"模拟视觉残留；铜铃用径向渐变做铜材质感，按铃时铃体与铃锤做衰减摆动、荡开两圈波纹、并触发鹈鹕点头。 - **声音零依赖**：铃声（三枚非谐波正弦叠加 + 双击节奏）和海浪环境声（布朗噪声 + 低通 + LFO 起伏）全部由 Web Audio 实时合成，右下角可静音。 - **晚霞海面**：半沉的落日拖出一条反光带，34 个波光点在其中以随机频率闪烁漂移，三层正弦海浪按视差流动；前景草丛、堤岸草、车道虚线、云、海鸟以不同速度向后掠过，营造持续的骑行前进感。 - **小彩蛋**：鹈鹕喉囊里藏着一条露尾的小鱼，随颠簸高频抖动；它会不时眨眼。点击画面任意处（或按空格）即可听一声铜铃。

PORT DE BRUME · 05:47

晨雾港口

一只鹈鹕，与它的清晨骑行

按住画面 —— 它会踩快一点

``` 实现说明： **单一相位驱动整个世界** —— 曲柄角 `theta` 是唯一的时钟：轮子转它的两倍速、踏板走 27px 半径的圆周、两条腿用两连杆逆运动学逐帧解出膝盖位置（髋部随身体起伏，脚锁定在踏板上）；背景滚动的线速度恰好等于轮缘线速度（`92·θ`），车轮与码头木板之间无相对滑动，远景、水面、浮标按 0.10 / 0.16 / 0.42 的系数做视差。 **喉囊律动** —— 喉囊以喙根为悬挂点，每踩一圈做一次 `scale(1, ±0.11)` 的鼓缩加 3px 的纵向浮动，头部同步轻微点头，与踩踏严格锁相，正是"用力一踩、喉囊一鼓"的节奏感。 **场景与细节** —— 两层雾中港口剪影（塔吊、拖船、灯塔、桅杆林）被地平线的晨雾拦腰截断；七只彩色浮标各自随波摇摆、灯球明灭；太阳光路用叠加混合在水面上碎成闪动的光斑；后货架绑着一条摆尾的鱼，前层灯柱和系缆柱会从鹈鹕身前掠过，制造一瞬的遮挡纵深。波纹、板缝等细节由种子 6768 的伪随机数铺排，右下角的"浮标 №6768"也埋了这个数。 **交互** —— 按住画面，踩踏频率平滑升至两倍，身体前倾、围巾扬平、视差整体加速；点一下鹈鹕，车铃"叮"地闪出弧线，喉囊还会猛地鼓一下。`prefers-reduced-motion` 下自动收敛为慢速静骑。

<script>
// 根据曲柄角度计算腿部（两段式 IK），使脚贴合踏板
const hip = {x: 395, y: 298};      // 相对于 translate(400) 前的坐标会在下面换算
const crank = {x: -5, y: 372}, R = 20;
const L1 = 42, L2 = 42;
const hipL = {x: -18, y: 296};
const near = document.getElementById('nearLeg');
const nearFoot = document.getElementById('nearFoot');
const farFoot = document.getElementById('farFoot');
const farLeg = document.getElementById('farLegPath');

function leg(angle){
  const p = {x: crank.x + R*Math.sin(angle), y: crank.y - R*Math.cos(angle)};
  const dx = p.x - hipL.x, dy = p.y - hipL.y;
  let d = Math.min(Math.hypot(dx, dy), L1 + L2 - 0.1);
  const a = Math.atan2(dy, dx);
  const b = Math.acos((L1*L1 + d*d - L2*L2) / (2*L1*d));
  const knee = {x: hipL.x + L1*Math.cos(a - b), y: hipL.y + L1*Math.sin(a - b)};
  return {p, knee};
}
function foot(p){
  return `M${p.x-6} ${p.y} L${p.x+14} ${p.y-4} L${p.x+16} ${p.y+3} L${p.x-6} ${p.y+4}Z`;
}
const start = performance.now();
function tick(t){
  const ang = ((t - start) / 1000) * Math.PI * 2; // 1 秒一圈，与曲柄同步
  const A = leg(ang), B = leg(ang + Math.PI);
  near.setAttribute('d', `M${hipL.x} ${hipL.y} L${A.knee.x} ${A.knee.y} L${A.p.x} ${A.p.y}`);
  nearFoot.setAttribute('d', foot(A.p));
  farLeg.setAttribute('d', `M${hipL.x} ${hipL.y} L${B.knee.x} ${B.knee.y} L${B.p.x} ${B.p.y}`);
  farFoot.setAttribute('d', foot(B.p));
  requestAnimationFrame(tick);
}
requestAnimationFrame(tick);
</script>

If a detail is uncertain, the card says that it is uncertain rather than presenting a guess as fact. The public display will open with a short map of the street, followed by three listening stations. Each station has headphones so that neighboring visitors can talk quietly without competing with loudspeakers. One interview describes a bakery that opened before sunrise; another recalls a repair shop where families brought lamps and radios. The third describes an annual neighborhood festival, but the librarian has asked the team not to use that anecdote as a precise date for the other businesses. The planning note gives the collection a project name: Juniper. That name was selected because it is easy to distinguish from the catalog numbers already used for books and recordings. It is a working label for the exhibition workflow, not the legal title of a donation or the name of a person who was interviewed. When the volunteers discuss file transfers with the library's digital preservation specialist, they should use the project name and the relevant catalog number together. One table will hold blank response cards for visitors who want to contribute memories of their own. The cards are optional and should not ask for more personal information than the library needs to follow up. A sealed box behind the desk will collect completed cards, and staff will review them before any details are added to the public website. The equipment list includes two spare headphone sets, a power strip approved by the facilities team, and a small sign explaining how to adjust volume.
